chunks: A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdillah from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Rib'i from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a bed that has gold in it; is it proper to keep it in the house? He said: 'If it is [made of] gold, then no [it is not proper/lawful]; and if it is 'water of gold' (gold-plated), then there is no harm [in keeping it].'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to keep gold-plated furniture in the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on luxury items by distinguishing between solid gold (*dhahab*) and gold-plated or gilded items (*ma' al-dhahab*). This distinction reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that excessive ostentation (*israf*) is discouraged, while the use of gold as a decorative coating remains permissible for household furnishings.
